newsitem.title: INDIA: Reliance sees Indian polyester demand up 22 pct.
newsitem.headline: Reliance sees Indian polyester demand up 22 pct.

text.p: Polyester major Reliance Industries Ltd on Friday said it expected Indian polyester staple fibre (PSF) demand to exceed 300,000 tonnes in 1996/97 (April-March), 22 percent up from the year-ago period.
"The demand/supply is expected to be balanced at around 300,000 tonnes," it said in a statement announcing the commissioning of a new 80,000 tonnes per year PSF plant.

"Reliance is expected to commission another 80,000 tonnes PSF plant within the next six months," it said. The PSF industry has shown a compounded growth rate in consumption of about 16 percent over the past 10 years, it said.

"It is expected that the total supply of PSF during 1997/98 will exceed 550,000 tonnes with Reliance continuing to dominate the industry," it said, adding Reliance expected to enhance its market share to nearly 55 percent in 1997/98 from 40 percent.
It said the international price of PSF rose by 15 percent to $1.10 per kg in recent weeks. Indian producers also raised prices to 57 rupees per kg from 52 rupees.
"In order to expand the market, domestic manufacturers have priced their products substantially cheaper than the international price," the statement said.
Reliance said it expected PSF consumption to increase because of very low prices which encourage substitution from cotton to polyester.
In India, polyester costs more than cotton. Indian cotton prices are about 20 percent cheaper than world prices.
"As and when the government allows the cotton growers to export, the Indian cotton prices will track the international prices. This will further enhance the consumption of PSF."
During the first six months of 1996/97 (April-March), around 20,000 tonnes of PSF was imported into India, Reliance said.
